# The second program's line 10 is CLEAR 10,33999!, which leaves it the stack
# that an MSX1 needs and little more. The Philips NMS 8250's BASIC needs 160
# free bytes at each check of the stack, where an MSX1's needs 120, and stops at
# "Out of memory in 40". The program opens a file, so it keeps its file's
# buffer. The patches write the program without the 63 spaces that BASIC does
# not need. The text ends earlier, and 1Ah, the end of an ASCII file, fills the
# rest of its block.
